Olvera Street merchants seek to join lawsuit over LA plaza's cross and Nativity display
LAX Leader
A group of merchants in Los Angeles is seeking to join a federal lawsuit in defense of a historic cross and Nativity display located at El Pueblo de Los Angeles, according to an Aug. 26 report.
The displays, which are within sight of each other at the city’s nearly-300-year-old center, have become the subject of legal action after resident Jack Gerritsen sued the city government. Gerritsen alleged that the displays violate the establishment clause of the U.S. Constitution by favoring specific religions and said they make him “feel excluded as a nonbeliever.” A U.S. district court initially ruled against Gerritsen, who has since appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit.
In an Aug. 24 filing, the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty asked the appeals court to allow Olvera Street merchants to intervene as defendants alongside the city. The filing stated that these business owners have “a significant and legally protected interest in preserving the historic and cultural heritage of El Pueblo” and “concrete economic interests in preserving the cross and nativity as important attractions that draw visitors to the area.”
The merchants say they help bring a “growing volume of visitors” interested in witnessing what they describe as “authentic and uninterrupted links” to Los Angeles’ historic past. The court filing also noted other local traditions such as La Iglesia de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles—a Catholic parish with roots dating back to 1784—and an annual Blessing of Animals event during Lent.
Edward Flores, one business owner on Olvera Street whose heritage includes Mexican Catholic roots, wrote, “Preserving our distinct cultures and educating others about our roles in the founding and growth of Los Angeles ennobles Americans across all ethnicities, faiths, cultures, and generations to take pride in their own contributions and to see more clearly their future potential.”
The Becket Fund’s filing suggested that existing court precedent may not find either display sufficiently "established" under constitutional standards regarding religious symbols on public property. It argued that "the longstanding and historic nature of the cross and nativity reflect[s] the precise nature of Merchants’ interests they seek to protect."
summary: Olvera Street merchants seek to join lawsuit over LA plaza's cross and Nativity display A group of merchants in Los Angeles is seeking to join a federal lawsuit in defense of a historic cross and Nativity display located at El Pueblo de Los Angeles, according to an Aug. 26 report. In an Aug. 24 filing, the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty asked the appeals court to allow Olvera Street merchants to intervene as defendants alongside the city.
